rv.q: This article is more than 12 years old Review Blithe Spirit review – Angela Lansbury's happy medium This article is more than 12 years old Gielgud, London The Broadway veteran plays a magnificently dotty Madame Arcati in this remarkable production of Coward's glacial comedy Quiz: Noël Coward or Murder, She Wrote?
Angela Lansbury’s return to the West End, after an absence of nearly 40 years, is something to treasure.
There's something weird, beautiful and disturbing about this Arcati, a lovable gorgon who's gone way beyond mere eccentricity.
Overall this is a wispy ectoplasm of the 1941. Noel Coward ghost comedy rather than a full-bodied materialization.
The veteran actress' portrayal of the endearing oddball medium who has unwittingly succeeded in bringing someone back from the dead was applauded at every exit and entrance.
Dame Angela is an absolute pro.

cn.t: Lansbury's triumphant return to the West End earns raves for her vivacious, Tony-winning turn as Madame Arcati, though critics find Blakemore's elegant revival occasionally stiff and lacking the full comedic spark of Coward's ghost comedy.
